prompt: A new analyst plans to answer "which stations ran out last week" by querying the dock sensors’ server every Monday. What goes wrong?

choices.text: The server answers no SQL, so there is no query to send it
choices.why: How it is asked is a detail; what it still holds is the problem.

choices.text: Five of the seven days she wants were deleted before she asks for them
choices.why: Right: the server keeps two days, so a week needs a copy kept elsewhere.

choices.text: The readings are in UTC, so the week comes out three hours shifted
choices.why: A clock can be converted; a reading that was deleted cannot be brought back.

choices.text: A reading a minute is too coarse to say when a station emptied
choices.why: A minute is fine enough for "for how long"; the history is what is missing.

prompt: The mechanics rename a column of their spreadsheet. The next load fills that column with empty values and reports success. In this course’s terms, what is that?

choices.text: A loud failure, since the empty column is plain to see
choices.why: Nothing stopped and nothing complained; somebody has to go and look to see it.

choices.text: A freshness problem: right data, arriving late
choices.why: The data arrived on time; what arrived is wrong.

choices.text: The quiet kind of failure, which nobody notices until a number is wrong
choices.why: Right: every dock now reads as unbroken and the load said it worked.

choices.text: The app team’s schema change, and so no failure of the load
choices.why: The spreadsheet is the mechanics’, and a load that reports success on a wrong result has failed.

prompt: Marta asks whether the price change in August made people ride less. In the table of roles, whose question is that?

choices.text: The analyst’s, since it is a question that has been asked
choices.why: The analyst answers with a number or a chart; whether a change caused a drop is an estimate of cause.

choices.text: The analytics engineer’s, who defines what a ride is
choices.why: The definition is needed first, and it does not answer the question.

choices.text: The data engineer’s, who has the rides
choices.why: He makes it answerable; somebody else answers it.

choices.text: The data scientist’s
choices.why: Right: an estimate of what caused what, as in "did the new pricing work".

prompt: A company collects and stores its data reliably, has no cleaned tables, and wants to run experiments on prices. Which level of Rogati’s pyramid has to be built next?

choices.text: aggregate and label
choices.why: That level rests on the one that has to come first.

choices.text: explore and transform
choices.why: Right: the third level, the last of the data engineer’s three.

choices.text: move and store
choices.why: The company already does that reliably.

choices.text: learn and optimise
choices.why: Experiments are this level: what they want, two levels above what they have.

prompt: A stream processor in 2025 reports seven rides on a morning that had six. Which of the four questions that have not changed in thirty years did it fail?

choices.text: Did all of it arrive?
choices.why: Nothing is missing; there is one too many.

choices.text: Is it what the source meant?
choices.why: Each ride is what the source said; one of them is there twice.

choices.text: Is it here in time?
choices.why: It arrived; it arrived too often.

choices.text: Did any of it arrive twice?
choices.why: Right: one ride counted twice, the `twice.py` failure.

prompt: By mistake, `first.py` is given the export for 13 September instead of the 14th. Its columns and rows are in order. What does it print?

choices.text: A `KeyError`, because the dates do not match the program
choices.why: A `KeyError` needs a missing column; the dates are values, and nothing reads them.

choices.text: Counts headed "on 14 September", printed with no complaint
choices.why: Right: the day is in the program’s text, not checked against the data. Nobody checked it was the right day.

choices.text: Zero rides, since none of them started on the 14th
choices.why: The program counts every row it is given, whatever its date.

choices.text: A refusal, since `started_at` disagrees with the title
choices.why: Nothing in it compares the two.

prompt: Why does lesson 1 say a pipeline is never finished, where an analysis is?

choices.text: Its code is too long to complete within one sprint
choices.why: Length has nothing to do with it; a ten-line pipeline runs tonight too.

choices.text: It runs again tonight, against a source that changes
choices.why: Right: it is software that runs every day.

choices.text: Its users keep asking it for new charts
choices.why: Charts are the analyst’s delivery, and each one is finished when delivered.

choices.text: Its tests are run in production
choices.why: That is not what the lesson says, nor a good habit.

prompt: Roda Livre’s data team is two people. Who does the analytics engineer’s work there?

choices.text: Marta, because she asks the questions

choices.text: A third hire, since the role needs a person of its own
choices.why: The roles name the work, not the people.

choices.text: Davi, who writes the SQL that defines a ride as well as the pipelines
choices.why: Right: the roles name the work, and in a team of two one person does several.

prompt: A job advert says the data engineer will "write the SQL the analysts need". What does lesson 1 say that picture leaves out?

choices.text: The dashboards those queries feed

choices.text: Python, which takes over where SQL stops
choices.why: Python is a skill too; the advert is wrong about the job, not about a language.

choices.text: Keeping one database fast and safe for its users
choices.why: That is a database administrator’s work, which the lesson separates from this one.

prompt: Marta never sees Davi’s work. When, according to lesson 1, does she notice it?

choices.text: When the morning check sends her its summary

choices.text: When it is absent: a report that is late or wrong
choices.why: Right: she sees only its absence.

choices.text: When she approves a new source for the platform

prompt: Payments last landed at 06:50. The team’s objective is two hours, and the agreement with the city is four hours at 09:00. What is the state at 09:00?

choices.text: An SLA breach, so the city earns a discount

choices.text: An SLO breach, while the promise made outside the team still holds

prompt: A matrix gives 36 to one option and 35 to another. What is the honest output?

choices.text: These two are equivalent on our criteria
choices.why: Right: the choice then goes to something the matrix does not hold.

choices.text: The first option, by a point
choices.why: One point is less than the doubt in any single score.

choices.text: Another round of scoring, until one leads by five
choices.why: That is scoring until the numbers agree with somebody, which launders a preference.

choices.text: More criteria, until the tie is broken
choices.why: Criteria added to break a tie are chosen for the result they give.

prompt: A matrix scores four options on "bill", "upkeep", "licence" and "support contract", and on one criterion for everything else. What is wrong with it?

choices.text: Four options are too many to compare in one matrix
choices.why: The number of options is not the trouble here.

choices.text: The weights were not shown to add up to ten
choices.why: Weights summing to ten was a convenience in `matrix.py`, not a rule.

choices.text: A scale of one to five is too coarse to separate them
choices.why: A finer scale would decide the same thing more precisely.

choices.text: Cost is counted four times
choices.why: Right: the matrix decided for the cheapest before anybody scored.

prompt: A colleague wants to move the rides into a new kind of database because "PostgreSQL will not scale". What does lesson 2 ask for before a token is spent?

choices.text: A measured fact about today, not a forecast about next year
choices.why: Right: "it took ten minutes this morning" is evidence; "it will not scale" is not.

choices.text: A benchmark published by the new database’s vendor
choices.why: That measures the vendor’s case, not Roda Livre’s.

choices.text: The agreement of the two most senior engineers
choices.why: Seniority is not evidence about this workload.

choices.text: A scoring matrix on which the new database wins
choices.why: A matrix built to win is the habit that spoils matrices.

prompt: A team builds its pipeline now and schedules "the security phase" for next quarter. What does lesson 2’s word "undercurrent" say about that?

choices.text: It is the right order once the pipeline works
choices.why: By then every copy has whatever the first stage let in, and it has to be found.

choices.text: Security is the question asked at each stage
choices.why: Right: it runs under every stage, not after them.

choices.text: It is enough if the raw zone is encrypted
choices.why: Who can read each table, at each stage, is the question; encryption at one place does not answer it.

choices.text: Security belongs to the cloud provider in a managed service
choices.why: The provider runs the software; who may read the payments is still the team’s decision.

prompt: In `cost.py`, "managed, every 5 min" pays 1226.12 a month in queries, each refresh reading the whole year. If each refresh read only the previous day instead, about what would that line become?

choices.text: About 0.01, like the plan that runs once a day
choices.why: That plan reads one day thirty times a month; this one reads one day 8,640 times.

choices.text: About 613, half as much
choices.why: The bytes read fall by a factor of 365, not 2.

choices.text: About 3.36
choices.why: Right: the same refreshes, each reading a 365th of the bytes.

choices.text: About 1226.12, since the number of refreshes is the same
choices.why: The engine charges for the bytes it reads, not for the refreshes.

prompt: Marta moves the false-start rule from two minutes to one. Raw files were deleted after thirty days. Which days can be rebuilt under the new rule?

choices.text: Every day, from the cleaned zone

choices.text: Every day, by asking the app’s database again
choices.why: The app keeps the present; a refunded ride has already been changed in place.

choices.text: Every day, from the curated counts

prompt: An analyst wants rides per station including false starts. Where should she get them?

choices.text: From the raw zone, since it holds every ride

choices.text: From a new curated table built from raw

choices.text: From the app’s database, since it is the source

choices.text: From the cleaned zone, after undoing the rule

prompt: The payments provider calls Roda Livre’s address each time a charge succeeds. The receiver was down for an hour. What happened to that hour’s charges?

choices.text: They are picked up by the next nightly pull
choices.why: Nothing pulls payments here; they are pushed.

choices.text: They wait in the raw zone until the receiver returns
choices.why: The raw zone is written by the receiver; with it down, nothing lands.

choices.text: Lost, unless the provider sends them again
choices.why: Right: with push, the source decides when, and the receiver must be listening.

choices.text: Recorded by ingestion with a gap marker
choices.why: Ingestion cannot mark what never reached it.

prompt: Suppose `trace.py` had printed curated 29, clean 29, raw 29 and app.db 31 for Rua XV. Which stage is suspected?

choices.text: Transformation

choices.text: Delivery
choices.why: The report matches curated.

choices.text: Generation
choices.why: The app holds 31; generation did its part.

choices.text: Ingestion
choices.why: Right: the copy should hold what the source held, and two rides are missing between them.

prompt: The app writes a ride when the bicycle is docked again, and `ingest.py` copies a day by `started_at` at 00:05. What becomes of a ride that starts on Monday at 23:50 and ends at 00:20?

choices.text: It is copied as an open ride with no end
choices.why: At 00:05 there is no row yet to copy.

choices.text: It is missed unless Monday is copied again
choices.why: Right: Monday’s copy ran before the row existed, and Tuesday’s copies Tuesday’s starts.

choices.text: It goes into Tuesday’s partition, when it ends
choices.why: The copy selects by when the ride started, and it started on Monday.

choices.text: It is copied twice, once into each day
choices.why: Neither day’s copy takes it.

prompt: Caio’s model wants one row per station per hour, with the rides and the weather. Which form of delivery is that?

choices.text: A report
choices.why: A report is read by a person at a fixed time.

choices.text: An API

choices.text: A feature table

prompt: Personal data arrives in the raw zone untouched. What does that make the decision of how long raw is kept?

choices.text: A decision for the source’s owner, who sent the data

choices.text: A decision about privacy, as much as one about cost and rebuilding

prompt: A log parser skips any line its pattern does not match. Overnight the web server’s log format changes. What does the next morning’s count of requests show?

choices.why: A parser that skips raises nothing.

choices.text: The same counts, since the fields are still in each line
choices.why: The pattern no longer matches, so no field is found.

choices.text: Half the requests, those still in the old format
choices.why: After the change, every line is in the new format.

choices.text: A day with no requests, and no error

prompt: An application event carries `occurred_at` from the phone, and the collector adds the time it arrived. How does lesson 4 say the two are used?

choices.text: Trust the phone’s, and ask about the collector’s

choices.text: Either, since the two differ by a second or two

prompt: A dock’s readings reach the server with sequence numbers 11, 12, 14, 13, 13. What does a loader keyed on sensor and sequence number count?

prompt: A partner drops its export in object storage, which has no rename. Which convention tells the reader the delivery is complete?

choices.text: Write under a temporary name, then rename
choices.why: That works on one filesystem; object storage has no rename to do it with.

choices.text: Wait until the file has stopped growing for a while
choices.why: A writer that died halfway also stops growing.

choices.text: A marker the writer adds last, like `_SUCCESS`
choices.why: Right: the reader touches nothing until it exists; a manifest also carries the rows and a checksum.

choices.text: Read the file twice and compare the two sizes
choices.why: Two equal sizes say nothing about whether the writer finished.

choices.text: "changes": announced thirty days ahead

choices.text: "personal_data": none

choices.text: "key": sensor_id and seq
choices.why: Right: two readings with one key are one reading.
